title: Foundry Agent Service map and agent types
summary: Foundry Agent Service is a managed platform with a runtime, toolboxes, models, tracing, optimization, identity and publishing. You choose how much you build: a prompt agent, a voice prompt agent, a hosted agent, or a direct Responses API call.
useIf: You are deciding where an agent should live in Foundry and want the map before the details.
avoidIf: You already know the agent type and need protocol, session or identity details: jump to the specific topic.

explain.md: Foundry Agent Service is a managed platform for building, deploying and scaling agents [[r1]]. Its parts are the **Agent Runtime** (hosts prompt and hosted agents, manages conversations and tool calls), **Toolboxes**, **Models** from the Foundry catalog, **Observability**, **Optimization**, **Identity and Security**, and **Publishing** [[r1]]. The runtime itself rests on three objects: an **agent** (model, instructions, tools), a **conversation** (persisted history) and a **response** (one unit of execution) [[tr1]]. A response can run with or without an agent or a conversation, so start with a response and add the others when you need them [[tr1]].

You then pick how much to build. A **prompt agent** is configuration only. A **voice-based prompt agent** adds managed real-time voice through Voice Live. A **hosted agent** is your own code, shipped as a container image or a .zip that Foundry builds into an image. Calling the **Responses API directly** from code you already run gives an *ephemeral agent*: the definition lives in your app and no Foundry agent resource exists [[r1]].

explain.title: Four ways in, one project endpoint
explain.alt: Clients reach prompt, voice and hosted agents through the Agent Runtime. Your own app can call the Responses API directly. All of them use the models and tools behind the project endpoint.
explain.src:
flowchart TB
  C[Client or channel] --> RT[Agent Runtime]
  RT --> PA[Prompt agent]
  RT --> VA[Voice prompt agent]
  RT --> HA[Hosted agent]
  APP[Your app, Responses API direct] --> M
  PA --> M[Models and toolbox]
  VA --> M
  HA --> M

explain.title: Resource model in one line
explain.md: The Foundry resource is `Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts` with kind `AIServices`, and a project is its subresource and the development boundary. Roles were renamed (Foundry User, Foundry Owner, Foundry Account Owner, Foundry Project Manager were Azure AI User, Azure AI Owner, Azure AI Account Owner, Azure AI Project Manager). Role IDs did not change [[r24]].

use: You want one managed place for runtime, tools, identity, tracing and publishing
You can accept Azure-hosted compute and the Foundry model catalog
You want to start light (prompt agent) and move to code only when a requirement forces it
avoid: Code must stay on another cloud or on premises and cannot move: self-host and only register it
You need a feature that is still preview and your policy forbids preview in production
A single prompt-only chatbot with no tools, identity or publishing needs: a direct model call is simpler
flips: A requirement for webhooks, custom protocols or persistent files flips a prompt agent to a hosted agent
An existing agent that already runs elsewhere flips you to the direct Responses API call or registration
A production ban on preview features removes voice-based agents and memory from the shortlist

pitfalls.symptom: Team builds a hosted agent for a simple FAQ bot
pitfalls.fix: Start with a prompt agent. The docs name it the least to manage and good for production agents without custom orchestration [[r1]].

pitfalls.symptom: A doc or sample refers to Connected Agents or a shared project endpoint with `agent_reference`
pitfalls.cause: Classic or initial-preview material that does not match the new service
pitfalls.fix: Check the date and the migration page. Connected Agents does not exist in the new service, and the initial-preview hosted backend ended on 2026-08-20 [[r11]].

pitfalls.symptom: Role assignment fails because the role name is not found
pitfalls.cause: Docs and portals mix old Azure AI names and new Foundry names
pitfalls.fix: Search for both names. The role IDs are unchanged [[r24]].

scenarios.title: Internal helper, small team
scenarios.situation: A team wants an internal assistant that answers from a few tools and a knowledge source. Nobody wants to own containers.
unknowns: Does any tool need to run inside our process?
Do we need Teams publishing later?
scenarios.question: Which entry point do you choose?

options.name: Prompt agent
options.why: Instructions, model and tools as configuration. Foundry runs it, with an Entra identity and a managed endpoint.
options.tradeoff: No custom code path, so a later need for webhooks or files means moving to a hosted agent.

options.name: Direct Responses API call
options.why: Keeps the definition in your repo and still uses Foundry models and tools.
options.tradeoff: You host and secure the calling process and get no Foundry agent resource to publish.

options.name: Hosted agent
options.why: It adds container build, compute billed per active session and code to maintain for a need that config covers.
options.tradeoff: Right when you need your own code, custom protocols or persistent files.

flips.if: The helper must receive webhooks from another system
flips.then: Hosted agent with the Invocations protocol.

flips.if: The definition must be reviewed and deployed with the app code

scenarios.takeaway: Default to the least to manage, and move up only when a named requirement forces it.

scenarios.title: Phone line, preview allowed
scenarios.situation: A business wants a spoken assistant for inbound calls. The team has no speech orchestration code and accepts preview features with a waiver.
unknowns: Do we need to inspect and redact the transcript between stages?
scenarios.question: How do you build it?

options.name: Voice-based prompt agent with Teams Phone extensibility or Twilio
options.why: Foundry manages the voice lifecycle through Voice Live, and Teams Phone extensibility and Twilio are the supported phone paths [[r1]].
options.tradeoff: Preview: no SLA. Direct SIP is not offered and evaluation covers full conversations only.

options.name: Hosted agent with Invocations WebSocket and your own voice stack
options.why: Full control over turn handling and tools, paired with Pipecat, LiveKit or Voice Live in the container [[r2]].
options.tradeoff: You write and operate the orchestration and pay for compute.

options.name: Prompt text agent behind a standard Teams card
options.why: The standard text-agent card is not shown for voice agents, and this does not give spoken turns [[r1]].
options.tradeoff: Fine for text chat, not for phone calls.

flips.if: Policy forbids preview features in production
flips.then: Hosted agent with Invocations WebSocket, after you confirm its status for your policy.

flips.if: Transcripts must be filtered between stages
flips.then: Use the cascaded architecture so text is inspectable.

scenarios.takeaway: Voice-based agents buy managed orchestration at the price of preview limits.

quiz.q: Which entry point leaves no Foundry agent resource and keeps the agent definition in your application code?
quiz.explain: An ephemeral agent is assembled in your process on each call. Prompt, hosted and voice agents are all persisted Foundry resources.

quiz.q: Match each entry point to the cost model the docs give for it.

pairs.r: Inference plus tools plus container compute

quiz.explain: The agent-type comparison table in the overview lists these cost models. Only the hosted agent adds container compute.

quiz.q: Which statements about status on 2026-10-13 are supported by the docs?
options: The agent optimizer is limited preview
Hosted agents have an explicit GA row in the Foundry GA table
Tracing is GA for prompt and hosted agents
quiz.explain: Voice agents and the optimizer carry preview labels and tracing is GA for prompt and hosted agents. The GA table has no separate hosted agent row, so an explicit hosted GA statement is unverified.

flashcards.front: Name the three Foundry agent types and the fourth entry point.
flashcards.back: Prompt agents, voice-based prompt agents and hosted agents. The fourth is calling the Responses API directly, which gives an ephemeral agent with no Foundry resource.

flashcards.front: What are the three runtime objects in Agent Service?
flashcards.back: Agent (model, instructions, tools), conversation (persisted history) and response (one execution). Start with a response and add the others when needed.
